minutes.headline: Water commissioners discussed PFAS costs, a cell-tower RFP and replacing an old dump truck; no formal decisions were recorded.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners heard that a PFAS funding grant application was submitted, that the AT&T lease on the Chase tank will go out to RFP, and that the district already has an infrastructure master plan. They discussed public criticism of water rates and PFAS costs, then reviewed quotes for replacing the old one-ton dump truck. The truck was left for commissioners to think over, and the meeting ended on a motion to adjourn.

budget_items.what_was_said: The engineering firm submitted the grant application; no word back and no timeline. Funding is reviewed on a rolling basis as applications arrive.

budget_items.topic: PFAS testing and master plan funding
budget_items.what_was_said: Reimbursement would provide funding for more testing, covering PFAS testing and an updated master plan. The figure in the captions is unclear.
The district counts as a small system based on the population it serves, not the whole town.

budget_items.topic: Cell tower lease RFP, Chase tank
budget_items.what_was_said: The AT&T agreement expires in about a year and a half; an RFP will go out for the tower space and the two highest bidders would be taken. AT&T wants to cut its rent.
Commissioners discussed public comments about a charge on bills tied to borrowing for the Massachusetts Avenue-area project, saying the vote was unanimous.
The superintendent got state-bid quotes for a Ford and a Dodge truck, with the Ford cheaper. Options include buying off state bid or going out to bid; the old truck would be traded in.

decisions.decision: Superintendent will send commissioners the truck quote information for them to consider; no choice of vehicle or purchase method was made.
The RFP for cell carriers on the Chase tank will be worded so the AT&T termination and access terms are clear; counsel is helping draft it.

what_happened.line: The Water District commissioners recorded no votes; the minutes note only a motion to adjourn and a motion on the September 25 minutes, with results not audible.
Commissioners left the replacement dump truck undecided; the superintendent will send them state-bid quote information for a Ford and a Dodge to consider.
The Chase tank cell-carrier lease will go out to RFP, worded to make the AT&T termination and access terms clear, with counsel helping draft it.
The engineering firm has submitted a PFAS grant application; there is no word back and no timeline, and funding is reviewed on a rolling basis.
Commissioners discussed public comments about a capital charge on bills tied to borrowing for the Massachusetts Avenue-area project, noting the original vote was unanimous.

why_it_matters: PFAS grant money, if awarded, would bear on how much of the cost of testing and treatment lands on water bills, and no decision on it is expected until the state responds.
The capital charge on water bills comes from borrowing for the Massachusetts Avenue-area project, so rates stay tied to that debt whatever the grant outcome.
The cell tower RFP and the truck purchase are the district's near-term spending choices; both are still open and neither has a recorded vote.
